name: Dimmer Switch (High Wattage)
description: A higher-capacity version of the Insteon wall dimmer switch, rated for up to 250 W of dimmable LED or 1,000 W of incandescent or halogen lighting. It can be controlled locally or remotely over Insteon.

steps.text: At the electrical panel, turn off the circuit breakers or remove the fuses feeding the wall box, and make sure the power is off.
Remove the wall plate from the old switch, unscrew the switch and gently pull it out.
Disconnect the wires from the switch.
Turn on power.
Use a voltage meter to identify the line and load wires that were connected to the switch, and identify the neutral and ground wires.
Turn off power.
Connect the wires: the bare switch wire to ground, white to neutral, red to load and black to line. Make sure the connections are firm with no exposed wire.
With the LEDs on the left, gently place the switch into the wall box and screw it into place.
Turn on power.
steps.expect: The switch and its load turn on.

steps.text: Tap the switch on and off to check that it works.
steps.expect: The switch and its load turn on and off.

steps.text: Reinstall the wall plate.

notes: In a multi-gang box next to another switch you may need to remove one or both pairs of metal heat sink tabs. Removing one pair derates the switch from 1000W to 800W; removing both pairs derates it to 600W.

In 3-way and 4-way circuits every switch must be replaced by an Insteon device. In the line box, the black wire goes to line plus one traveler and the red wire is capped; in the load box, the black wire goes to the line-carrying traveler and the red wire to load. Then link all the switches as a group.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.

notes: As a controller: after the switch beeps, set the responder to the desired brightness or state and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps. The switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking. Repeat for each responder.
As a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, set the switch to the desired brightness, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.
A link is one way. To keep two switches in sync (a group, as in a 3-way circuit), link them in both directions.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.
Once linked, the Hub reads the device's settings with Get Operating Flags and an extended Get for group 1.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the responder's SET button until it double-beeps.
steps.expect: The switch double-beeps and its LED stops blinking.

notes: To remove the switch as a responder: press and hold the controller button until it beeps, press and hold it again until it beeps, then press and hold the switch's SET button until it double-beeps.

steps.text: Pull out the SET button to remove power.
Wait 5 seconds.
Push in the SET button and hold it. Do not let go.
When the long beep stops, release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the switch double-beeps and the load turns on.

verification.note: The Dimmer Switch 2477DH Owner's Manual (rev 7.0+) says to wait 5 seconds with the SET button pulled out; the later Dimmer Switch 2477D Owner's Manual, which covers the 2477S, 2477D and 2477DH, says about ten seconds. The catalog uses the Dimmer Switch 2477DH Owner's Manual's 5 seconds.

steps.text: Remove the switch as a responder from every controller that controls it.
Take the switch out of use.

notes: Otherwise its controllers will keep retrying commands, creating network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0; the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

notes: The Dimmer Switch 2477DH Owner's Manual prints subcategory 0x20, the 2477D's; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives the 2477DH 0x01/0x2D for every revision.
